Particle-based Generalised Stochastic Optimisation

The paper’s notation and assumptions, four main proved theorems, and two new time-uniform discretisation bounds, each beside its Lean formalization.

Preprint source; checked theorems and new unpublished bounds

The correspondence uses arXiv:2608.02844v2, identical to the manuscript audited here. The four main theorems of the paper are proved under its assumptions A1–A5, the extra assumptions Extra A1–Extra A3 and explicit solution interpretations: A2 is read as stationary weak frozen invariance, and constant-diffusion contraction uses the finite signed-work convention. The time-uniform discretisation bounds New A and New B for M-MFPO and HOL-MYPGD, with explicit constants, are new and unpublished. The source audit records these interpretations and the printed HOL coefficient defect.

  • Jiechen Jackie Zhang and O. Deniz Akyildiz (2026). Particle-based Generalised Stochastic Optimisation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.02844, version 2 (9 October 2026). Full paper

Exact shared imports, variables and namespace context

All module context commands are shown in source order, with declaration bodies omitted. The complete module on the linked proof page preserves their scope.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic

/-!
# The general particle-based gradient stochastic optimisation framework

`Model` has independent optimiser, parameter, sampler, observation and noise
coordinate types. In particular neither the optimiser nor the sampler is
restricted to a first-order gradient flow. Auxiliary momenta and adaptive
optimiser variables belong to `S`; augmented sampler variables belong to `Z`.

`IsWeakSolution` states the actual optimiser ODE and weak Fokker--Planck
equation. It is a law-level solution notion. No existence, equivalence to a
strong SDE, or stochastic Itô formula is asserted by this file.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal

namespace PBGSO

variable {S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [NormedSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [NormedSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [Fintype I]

/-- The `P₂` condition on a sampler law. Probability normalisation is
specified separately, so this predicate records exactly the moment input. -/

/-- The paper's independent optimiser and sampler design choices. A finite
noise index specifies the columns of the diffusion matrix. -/

namespace Model

variable (M : Model S Θ Z X I)

/-- `G_ν(ϑ)`, with an actual Bochner integral over the full sampler state. -/

/-- The full optimiser vector field driven by a sampler law. -/

/-- The interacting-particle gradient. All particles share the same complete
optimiser state. Bounds use `0 < N`, since no gradient estimate exists for an
empty particle population. -/

/-- The sampler empirical measure. At positive population size its total
mass is one; zero population is excluded by all sampling estimates. -/

/-- The finite-sum gradient is exactly integration against the empirical
law, rather than an independent primitive estimator. -/

/-- The augmented invariant law has the intended gradient expectation as
soon as its observation projection has the target marginal. -/

/-- The empirical law is a probability law for positive particle count. -/

/-- The continuous-time particle vector field, before time discretisation. -/

/-- An Euler step for an arbitrary optimiser response and sampler. `noise`
contains Brownian increments, with their scaling already included. -/

/-- The frozen sampler generator, including state- and parameter-dependent
diffusion. The two Fréchet derivatives are evaluated in sampler coordinates. -/

/-- A weak law solution for a specified separating test family. This makes
the analytic solution notion explicit instead of assuming an error bound.
Integrability is required rather than relying on totalised integrals. -/

/-- Frozen stationarity stated at the infinitesimal generator level. This
is an analytic input: boundary conditions and generator-domain arguments
must establish it for a proposed Gibbs diffusion. -/

/-- Uniqueness is quantified over the explicit ODE/forward equation above.
It is a well-posedness assumption, not a stationarity conclusion. -/

/-- Paper Theorem 1, candidate part: a vanishing exact gradient, a fixed
optimiser state, and a frozen invariant sampler make a constant weak
solution. Time-dependent optimiser responses are allowed. -/

/-- Paper Theorem 1 at the explicit weak-solution level. The only analytic
inputs are frozen generator stationarity, integrability and uniqueness. -/

/-- The gradient identity makes every stationary point suitable for the
previous stationarity theorem. It does not assert global minimality. -/

/-- Relabelling particles does not change their common gradient estimate. -/

end Model
end PBGSO

Exact shared imports, variables and namespace context

import PBGSO.Framework
import Mathlib.Analysis.ODE.Gronwall
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
# Quantitative comparison arguments for PBGSO

The model and joint monotonicity definition retain general optimiser maps,
augmented sampler states, and multiplicative noise. The comparison theorems
below prove the deterministic analytic step of the paper's arguments from
explicit energy derivative hypotheses. Identifying such derivatives with
coupled stochastic laws requires a separate Itô/martingale argument; that
argument is not silently included in these hypotheses or claimed here.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators RealInnerProductSpace InnerProductSpace Topology

namespace PBGSO

section Geometry
variable {S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [InnerProductSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [Fintype I]

/-- Explicit positive-definite quadratic weights and their spectral bounds.
No symmetry or definiteness is inferred from an arbitrary matrix. -/

namespace TwistedGeometry
variable (D : TwistedGeometry S Z)





end TwistedGeometry

/-- The two marginals are specified by genuine pushforwards. -/

/-- The sampler contribution to the twisted quadratic coupling energy.
The sum is the weighted Hilbert--Schmidt diffusion correction. -/

/-- The exact twisted joint strong monotonicity assumption in the paper,
including the Hilbert--Schmidt diffusion correction represented by its
finite sum of squared column norms. The gradient integrability premises
exclude accidental use of undefined Bochner expectations. -/

end Geometry

/-- Grönwall proves the squared-energy decay from a right derivative
inequality. This theorem applies to any energy, including an expectation
once differentiation under the stochastic integral has been justified. -/

/-- The square-root comparison needed for the finite-particle theorem.
It is proved from the *squared* energy inequality and zero initial error.
No differentiability of `sqrt E` at its zeros is assumed: the proof uses
`sqrt (E + ε²)` and then sends `ε` to zero by an order argument. -/

/-- The condition-number factor follows from the two quadratic norm
comparisons; the estimate is on the root mean square distance. -/

/-- The diagonal-dominance sufficient condition in Appendix A. It controls
the optimiser--sampler cross term as part of one joint quadratic form. -/

/-- A sharp completion-of-squares criterion for the 2×2 small-gain matrix.
It can be used with any certified lower eigenvalue `ρ`. -/

/-- Combining particle interaction and mean-field relaxation gives the
paper's parameter bound; the triangle premise is explicitly separate. -/

/-- The exponential relaxation factor tends to zero at every positive
contractivity rate. -/

/-- A finite distance between two stationary solutions is zero if the

/-!
# Quantitative comparison arguments for PBGSO

The model and joint monotonicity definition retain general optimiser maps,
augmented sampler states, and multiplicative noise. The comparison theorems
below prove the deterministic analytic step of the paper's arguments from
explicit energy derivative hypotheses. Identifying such derivatives with
coupled stochastic laws requires a separate Itô/martingale argument; that
argument is not silently included in these hypotheses or claimed here.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators RealInnerProductSpace InnerProductSpace Topology

namespace PBGSO

section Geometry
variable {S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [InnerProductSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [Fintype I]

/-- Explicit positive-definite quadratic weights and their spectral bounds.
No symmetry or definiteness is inferred from an arbitrary matrix. -/

namespace TwistedGeometry
variable (D : TwistedGeometry S Z)





end TwistedGeometry

/-- The two marginals are specified by genuine pushforwards. -/

/-- The sampler contribution to the twisted quadratic coupling energy.
The sum is the weighted Hilbert--Schmidt diffusion correction. -/

/-- The exact twisted joint strong monotonicity assumption in the paper,
including the Hilbert--Schmidt diffusion correction represented by its
finite sum of squared column norms. The gradient integrability premises
exclude accidental use of undefined Bochner expectations. -/

end Geometry

/-- Grönwall proves the squared-energy decay from a right derivative
inequality. This theorem applies to any energy, including an expectation
once differentiation under the stochastic integral has been justified. -/

/-- The square-root comparison needed for the finite-particle theorem.
It is proved from the *squared* energy inequality and zero initial error.
No differentiability of `sqrt E` at its zeros is assumed: the proof uses
`sqrt (E + ε²)` and then sends `ε` to zero by an order argument. -/

/-- The condition-number factor follows from the two quadratic norm
comparisons; the estimate is on the root mean square distance. -/

/-- The diagonal-dominance sufficient condition in Appendix A. It controls
the optimiser--sampler cross term as part of one joint quadratic form. -/

/-- A sharp completion-of-squares criterion for the 2×2 small-gain matrix.
It can be used with any certified lower eigenvalue `ρ`. -/

/-- Combining particle interaction and mean-field relaxation gives the
paper's parameter bound; the triangle premise is explicitly separate. -/

/-- The exponential relaxation factor tends to zero at every positive
contractivity rate. -/

/-- A finite distance between two stationary solutions is zero if the
same contraction estimate holds for every nonnegative elapsed time. -/

/-- The explicit right-hand side of the paper's parameter estimate has the
stated long-time sampling floor. No discretisation term is included. -/

/-- The sampling floor vanishes as the number of particles tends to
infinity, with all geometry and variance constants fixed. -/

end PBGSO

/-! # Source stationarity in the actual local strong-equation class
The stochastic noise is the constructed local Brownian integral, not a free
interpretation operator. Only pathwise time-L¹ drift and local square diffusion
are required. Source A1 is exposed as same-driver pathwise uniqueness in this
class; actual frozen invariance is source A2. Neither an energy identity nor
time-L¹(L²) drift is used in the stationarity argument.
-/

  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [NormedSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ] [CompleteSpace Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z] [CompleteSpace Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [BorelSpace Z] [SecondCountableTopology Z]
  (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
  (D : Driver (I := I) Q) (M : Model S Θ Z X I) (T : ℝ≥0)

/-- Original raw sampler equation with actual constructed local Brownian
noise. The local coefficients may be normalized on a common null event;
their realization as the original model coefficients is stated explicitly.
Pathwise Bochner integrability does not imply a time-L¹(L²) assumption here. -/

/-- Original mean-field optimiser integral ODE and actual local sampler equation.
The marginal P₂/observation domains are explicit source assumptions. -/

/-- The same-driver uniqueness conclusion needed from source A1, now for
actual computed local integrals. It quantifies over local energy choices and
common-null coefficient realizations, rather than assuming identical gauges. -/

/-- Source A2 as an actual invariant frozen sampler trajectory satisfying
the original locally integrable SDE. Its original optimiser is not supplied:
the constant optimiser solution is constructed from the zero-gradient rule. -/

variable {Q D M T}

/-- Normalization is derived from the actual invariant frozen output. -/

/-- The frozen invariant law's second moment follows from its original
initial L² variable; no all-time coefficient moment is assumed. -/

/-- The zero optimiser drift is proved from actual frozen invariance,
zero mean gradient and the optimiser fixed point. The original local sampler
equation is retained verbatim, including arbitrary multiplicative diffusion. -/

/-- Source invariant-measure conclusion using the actual local Brownian
integral and only source pathwise uniqueness, frozen invariance, zero gradient
and optimiser fixed-point assumptions. No stronger drift moment or energy
hypothesis is introduced. -/

/-- Literal complete-state stationary product law. Optimiser and sampler
auxiliary variables remain in their original state spaces. -/

end PBGSO.RawLocalStationarity

end WeakFrozen
end PBGSO.RawLocalStationarity

Interpretation of A2 — Actual stationary weak SDE

Mathematical statement

Source: Jiechen Jackie Zhang and O. Deniz Akyildiz (2026), A2 (the frozen invariant law).

Frozen invariance means an actual stationary weak frozen SDE on some filtered Brownian probability space. Its paths are continuous and adapted, and satisfy

Zt=Z0+∫0tbθ⋆(Zr) dr+∫0tσθ⋆(Zr) dBr,Law⁡(Zt)=νθ⋆.Z_t=Z_0+\int_0^t b_{\theta_\star}(Z_r)\,\mathrm dr+\int_0^t\sigma_{\theta_\star}(Z_r)\,\mathrm dB_r,\qquad\operatorname{Law}(Z_t)=\nu_{\theta_\star}.Zt​=Z0​+∫0t​bθ⋆​​(Zr​)dr+∫0t​σθ⋆​​(Zr​)dBr​,Law(Zt​)=νθ⋆​​.
Zt=Z0+∫0tbθ⋆(Zr) dr+∫0tσθ⋆(Zr) dBr,Law⁡(Zt)=νθ⋆.\begin{gathered}Z_t=Z_0+\int_0^t b_{\theta_\star}(Z_r)\,\mathrm dr\\\quad+\int_0^t\sigma_{\theta_\star}(Z_r)\,\mathrm dB_r,\\\operatorname{Law}(Z_t)=\nu_{\theta_\star}.\end{gathered}Zt​=Z0​+∫0t​bθ⋆​​(Zr​)dr+∫0t​σθ⋆​​(Zr​)dBr​,Law(Zt​)=νθ⋆​​.​

This may be a different probability space from the coupled strong solution. A generator identity alone does not supply this solution premise.

/-!
# Quantitative comparison arguments for PBGSO

The model and joint monotonicity definition retain general optimiser maps,
augmented sampler states, and multiplicative noise. The comparison theorems
below prove the deterministic analytic step of the paper's arguments from
explicit energy derivative hypotheses. Identifying such derivatives with
coupled stochastic laws requires a separate Itô/martingale argument; that
argument is not silently included in these hypotheses or claimed here.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators RealInnerProductSpace InnerProductSpace Topology

namespace PBGSO

section Geometry
variable {S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [InnerProductSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [Fintype I]

/-- Explicit positive-definite quadratic weights and their spectral bounds.
No symmetry or definiteness is inferred from an arbitrary matrix. -/

namespace TwistedGeometry
variable (D : TwistedGeometry S Z)





end TwistedGeometry

/-- The two marginals are specified by genuine pushforwards. -/

/-- The sampler contribution to the twisted quadratic coupling energy.
The sum is the weighted Hilbert--Schmidt diffusion correction. -/

/-- The exact twisted joint strong monotonicity assumption in the paper,
including the Hilbert--Schmidt diffusion correction represented by its
finite sum of squared column norms. The gradient integrability premises
exclude accidental use of undefined Bochner expectations. -/

end Geometry

/-- Grönwall proves the squared-energy decay from a right derivative
inequality. This theorem applies to any energy, including an expectation
once differentiation under the stochastic integral has been justified. -/

/-- The square-root comparison needed for the finite-particle theorem.
It is proved from the *squared* energy inequality and zero initial error.
No differentiability of `sqrt E` at its zeros is assumed: the proof uses
`sqrt (E + ε²)` and then sends `ε` to zero by an order argument. -/

/-- The condition-number factor follows from the two quadratic norm
comparisons; the estimate is on the root mean square distance. -/

/-- The diagonal-dominance sufficient condition in Appendix A. It controls
the optimiser--sampler cross term as part of one joint quadratic form. -/

/-- A sharp completion-of-squares criterion for the 2×2 small-gain matrix.
It can be used with any certified lower eigenvalue `ρ`. -/

/-- Combining particle interaction and mean-field relaxation gives the
paper's parameter bound; the triangle premise is explicitly separate. -/

/-- The exponential relaxation factor tends to zero at every positive
contractivity rate. -/

/-- A finite distance between two stationary solutions is zero if the
same contraction estimate holds for every nonnegative elapsed time. -/

/-- The explicit right-hand side of the paper's parameter estimate has the
stated long-time sampling floor. No discretisation term is included. -/

/-- The sampling floor vanishes as the number of particles tends to
infinity, with all geometry and variance constants fixed. -/

end PBGSO

Extra A2 — finite signed work for constant-diffusion contraction

Mathematical statement

For every optimiser pair and every joint probability law with finite quadratic moment, require the ordinary finite signed-integral domain:

∫∣⟨z−z~,Dz[bΠθϑ(z)−bΠθϑ~(z~)]⟩∣ Λ(dz,dz~)<∞.\int\left|\langle z-\tilde z,D_z[b_{\Pi_\theta\vartheta}(z)-b_{\Pi_\theta\tilde\vartheta}(\tilde z)]\rangle\right|\,\Lambda(\mathrm dz,\mathrm d\tilde z)<\infty.∫​⟨z−z~,Dz​[bΠθ​ϑ​(z)−bΠθ​ϑ~​(z~)]⟩​Λ(dz,dz~)<∞.
Δb=bΠθϑ(z)−bΠθϑ~(z~),∫∣⟨z−z~,DzΔb⟩∣ dΛ<∞.\begin{gathered}\Delta b=b_{\Pi_\theta\vartheta}(z)-b_{\Pi_\theta\tilde\vartheta}(\tilde z),\\\int|\langle z-\tilde z,D_z\Delta b\rangle|\,\mathrm d\Lambda<\infty.\end{gathered}Δb=bΠθ​ϑ​(z)−bΠθ​ϑ~​(z~),∫∣⟨z−z~,Dz​Δb⟩∣dΛ<∞.​

The Lean integrand also contains the weighted Hilbert–Schmidt diffusion term of A3; it vanishes under constant diffusion, the only branch that uses Extra A2. This FiniteCouplingWork condition is used for the constant-diffusion branch of Theorem 2 and its stationary uniqueness corollary. It strengthens an extended-negative-work reading of A3; it is not imposed separately on Theorems 3 or 4.

Each frozen drift and diffusion column is Borel, and Πθ\Pi_\thetaΠθ​ is continuous. Along the canonical strong solutions, the functions

(r,ω)↦bΠθϑr(Zr(ω)),(r,ω)↦σΠθϑr(Zr(ω))ei(r,\omega)\mapsto b_{\Pi_\theta\vartheta_r}(Z_r(\omega)),\qquad(r,\omega)\mapsto\sigma_{\Pi_\theta\vartheta_r}(Z_r(\omega))e_i(r,ω)↦bΠθ​ϑr​​(Zr​(ω)),(r,ω)↦σΠθ​ϑr​​(Zr​(ω))ei​
(r,ω)↦bΠθϑr(Zr(ω)),(r,ω)↦σΠθϑr(Zr(ω))ei\begin{gathered}(r,\omega)\mapsto b_{\Pi_\theta\vartheta_r}(Z_r(\omega)),\\(r,\omega)\mapsto\sigma_{\Pi_\theta\vartheta_r}(Z_r(\omega))e_i\end{gathered}(r,ω)↦bΠθ​ϑr​​(Zr​(ω)),(r,ω)↦σΠθ​ϑr​​(Zr​(ω))ei​​

are jointly strongly measurable, and the drift is progressively strongly measurable with respect to the driver filtration. The linear-growth inequality is exactly A1(ii). These are extra measurability assumptions; the proof derives the moment and energy estimates.

Theorem 1

Mathematical statement

Source: Jiechen Jackie Zhang and O. Deniz Akyildiz (2026), Theorem 1.

Assumptions: A1, A2, with the actual weak-SDE meaning stated above. Initialise the optimiser at the target and the sampler independently of Brownian motion with its frozen invariant law.

Extra assumptions: none.

For every t≥0t\ge0t≥0,

Law⁡(ϑt,Zt)=μ⋆:=δϑ⋆⊗νθ⋆.\operatorname{Law}(\vartheta_t,Z_t)=\mu_\star:=\delta_{\vartheta_\star}\otimes\nu_{\theta_\star}.Law(ϑt​,Zt​)=μ⋆​:=δϑ⋆​​⊗νθ⋆​​.
Law⁡(ϑt,Zt)=μ⋆,μ⋆:=δϑ⋆⊗νθ⋆.\begin{gathered}\operatorname{Law}(\vartheta_t,Z_t)=\mu_\star,\\\mu_\star:=\delta_{\vartheta_\star}\otimes\nu_{\theta_\star}.\end{gathered}Law(ϑt​,Zt​)=μ⋆​,μ⋆​:=δϑ⋆​​⊗νθ⋆​​.​

For time-dependent optimiser response this asserts a stationary solution; for autonomous response it is also ordinary invariant-measure preservation.

The state has the Euclidean product norm (`WithLp 2`), not the default

exactly its squared distance to the quadratic transport cost.

state. Auxiliary optimiser and sampler variables are retained. -/

/-- Every optimiser coordinate under the actual product law is s. -/

/-- Lift a genuine sampler coupling to the full two product laws. -/

/-- Project any genuine full-state coupling to its sampler marginals. -/

/-- The full quadratic cost decomposes into deterministic optimiser cost
and projected sampler cost on any actual coupling of the two product laws. -/



/-- Exact Wasserstein identity for the actual deterministic-optimiser
product laws, with the Euclidean product norm and finite second moments.
No optimal-coupling existence or supplied product-transport identity is used. -/

end ProductTransport

Theorem 3 — Finite-particle interaction error

Mathematical statement

Source: Jiechen Jackie Zhang and O. Deniz Akyildiz (2026), Theorem 3.

Assumptions: A1, A3–A5; positive population; deterministic optimiser initialisation; i.i.d. initial samplers from a common second-moment law, independent of the independent Brownian drivers; and an actual interacting solution of the original native SDE.

Extra assumption: Extra A1.

Couple the particle and independent-copy systems synchronously: ϑ0N=ϑˉ0\vartheta_0^N=\bar\vartheta_0ϑ0N​=ϑˉ0​, Z0i=Zˉ0iZ_0^i=\bar Z_0^iZ0i​=Zˉ0i​, with the same driver for each pair. Put νˉt[N]=N−1∑iδZˉti\bar\nu_t^{[N]}=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{\bar Z_t^i}νˉt[N]​=N−1∑i​δZˉti​​.

For every t≥0t\ge0t≥0,

∥d((ϑtN,νtN),(ϑˉt,νˉt[N]))∥L2≤LΨρκVFN(1−e−ρt).\begin{gathered}\left\|\mathbf d((\vartheta_t^N,\nu_t^N),(\bar\vartheta_t,\bar\nu_t^{[N]}))\right\|_{\mathrm L^2}\\\le\frac{L_\Psi}{\rho}\sqrt{\frac{\kappa V_F}{N}}(1-e^{-\rho t}).\end{gathered}​d((ϑtN​,νtN​),(ϑˉt​,νˉt[N]​))​L2​≤ρLΨ​​NκVF​​​(1−e−ρt).​

The comparison is with the independent-copy empirical law. A population-law Wasserstein estimate also needs empirical sampling error.

import PBGSO.GeneralProcess

/-!
# Pointwise L² lifting of the original finite-particle implementation forces

The optimiser is a random coordinate on the same probability space as every
particle. The cloud encoding is an explicit continuous linear equivalence;
it permits a Euclidean Gaussian cloud to represent the paper's particle array.
The empirical force and sampler force are constructed from the original `F`
and `G`. Their pointwise identification is proved, not postulated.
-/
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal ENNReal
namespace PBGSO.Methods

section Pair

  [NormedAddCommGroup C] [NormedSpace ℝ C]
  (Q : Measure Ω)

/-- Pair two random variables on their shared probability space, retaining
all dependence between the optimiser and the particle cloud. -/

/-- The L² pairing is the actual pointwise pair almost everywhere. -/



/-- The joint L² difference is controlled by the sum of marginal L² norms;
no independence between those marginals is used. -/

/-- Evaluate a pair of L² coordinates on their shared sample. -/

/-- Evaluate both momentum and position coordinates. -/

Mathematical statement

Take N≥1N\ge1N≥1, deterministic initial optimiser state, and i.i.d. initial sampler states with common law ν0∈P2\nu_0\in\mathcal P_2ν0​∈P2​, independently of the independent Brownian drivers. Assume A3 with ρ>0\rho>0ρ>0, A5 with VF≥0V_F\ge0VF​≥0, and target zero mean observation Gνθ⋆(ϑ⋆)=0G_{\nu_{\theta_\star}}(\vartheta_\star)=0Gνθ⋆​​​(ϑ⋆​)=0 for the chosen complete-state model.

Use the physical noise from the paper: 2γ dBi\sqrt{2\gamma}\,\mathrm dB^i2γ​dBi for M-MFPO, and 2α dBi\sqrt{2\alpha}\,\mathrm dB^i2α​dBi in the final HOL auxiliary coordinate. The optimiser receives no thermal noise.

Extra A5 — canonical frozen-target realization

Mathematical statement

For the target pair, require νθ⋆∈P2\nu_{\theta_\star}\in\mathcal P_2νθ⋆​​∈P2​. On νθ⋆\nu_{\theta_\star}νθ⋆​​ times the canonical Brownian probability, supply a norm-continuous L2\mathrm L^2L2 frozen sampler trajectory, initialized by the initial-coordinate projection, which satisfies

Zt⋆−Z0⋆=∫0tbθ⋆(Zr⋆) dr+σ⋆Bt,Law⁡(Zt⋆)=νθ⋆(t≥0).Z_t^\star-Z_0^\star=\int_0^t b_{\theta_\star}(Z_r^\star)\,\mathrm dr+\sigma_\star B_t,\qquad\operatorname{Law}(Z_t^\star)=\nu_{\theta_\star}\quad(t\ge0).Zt⋆​−Z0⋆​=∫0t​bθ⋆​​(Zr⋆​)dr+σ⋆​Bt​,Law(Zt⋆​)=νθ⋆​​(t≥0).
Zt⋆−Z0⋆=∫0tbθ⋆(Zr⋆) dr+σ⋆Bt,Law⁡(Zt⋆)=νθ⋆(t≥0).\begin{gathered}Z_t^\star-Z_0^\star=\int_0^t b_{\theta_\star}(Z_r^\star)\,\mathrm dr+\sigma_\star B_t,\\\operatorname{Law}(Z_t^\star)=\nu_{\theta_\star}\quad(t\ge0).\end{gathered}Zt⋆​−Z0⋆​=∫0t​bθ⋆​​(Zr⋆​)dr+σ⋆​Bt​,Law(Zt⋆​)=νθ⋆​​(t≥0).​

The constant physical diffusion is the one in the numerical initialization. This explicit FrozenTrajectory input is stronger than the weak frozen-SDE realization used in Theorem 1. The numerical endpoint retains it as a visible assumption.

import PBGSO.AdditiveCanonicalRealization
import PBGSO.NumericsTarget

/-! # Actual frozen invariance builds the additive stationary target data

The frozen sampler input is an actual continuous L² trajectory with its
integral equation and constant output law. This is the source frozen
invariance assumption, not a conclusion inferred from an empty test family.
Its constant optimiser extension is derived, primitive uniqueness identifies
the canonical target process, and every initial coupling is then realized by
the already constructed product extension. No relaxation bound or realizer
is a hypothesis.
-/

namespace PBGSO

variable {Ξ A G Z X I : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ξ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [InnerProductSpace ℝ A] [CompleteSpace A]
  [MeasurableSpace A] [BorelSpace A] [SecondCountableTopology A]
  [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] [CompleteSpace G]
  [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G] [SecondCountableTopology G]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z] [CompleteSpace Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [BorelSpace Z] [SecondCountableTopology Z] [Fintype I]
  (R : Measure Ξ) [IsProbabilityMeasure R]
  (L : LipschitzDynamics A Z G) (M : Model A G Z X I)
  (H : AdditiveModelCompatibility L M)
  (νStar : Measure Z) [IsProbabilityMeasure νStar]
  (hνStar : MemLp (fun z : Z => z) 2 νStar) (aStar : A)
  (B : ℝ → Lp Z 2 R) (hB : Continuous B) (hB0 : B 0 = 0)

/-- Actual frozen invariant dynamics with the model's sampler drift and the
same initial-law/noise source as the canonical construction. -/

variable (F : FrozenTrajectory R L νStar hνStar aStar B)
include H F

/-- The optimiser's zero observation follows from the actual frozen law. -/

/-- The fixed optimiser plus the actual frozen sampler satisfy the complete
mean-field integral equation; optimiser stationarity is derived. -/

/-- The canonical target flow has the actual stationary optimiser and law;
this is proved by primitive same-input uniqueness against the frozen flow. -/

/-- The actual frozen invariant trajectory builds every stationary-target
process premise used by the finite-particle/numerical theorem. In particular,
its all-initial-couplings realizer is a conclusion of the construction. -/

end AdditiveStationary
end PBGSO

The two method models and their raw coordinates

Mathematical statement

As in the paper’s algorithm section, suppress the population superscript in the method coordinates. For M-MFPO:

θ˙t=mt,m˙t=−N−1∑iF(θt,Xti)−γmt,dXti=Vti dt,dVti=(−Fx(θt,Xti)−γVti) dt+2γ dBti.\begin{aligned}\dot\theta_t&=m_t,\qquad\dot m_t=-N^{-1}\sum_i F(\theta_t,X_t^i)-\gamma m_t,\\\mathrm dX_t^i&=V_t^i\,\mathrm dt,\\\mathrm dV_t^i&=(-F_x(\theta_t,X_t^i)-\gamma V_t^i)\,\mathrm dt+\sqrt{2\gamma}\,\mathrm dB_t^i.\end{aligned}θ˙t​dXti​dVti​​=mt​,m˙t​=−N−1i∑​F(θt​,Xti​)−γmt​,=Vti​dt,=(−Fx​(θt​,Xti​)−γVti​)dt+2γ​dBti​.​
θ˙t=mt,m˙t=−N−1∑iF(θt,Xti)−γmt,dXti=Vti dt,dVti=(−Fx(θt,Xti)−γVti) dt+2γ dBti.\begin{aligned}\dot\theta_t&=m_t,\\\dot m_t&=-N^{-1}\sum_i F(\theta_t,X_t^i)-\gamma m_t,\\\mathrm dX_t^i&=V_t^i\,\mathrm dt,\\\mathrm dV_t^i&=(-F_x(\theta_t,X_t^i)-\gamma V_t^i)\,\mathrm dt\\&\quad+\sqrt{2\gamma}\,\mathrm dB_t^i.\end{aligned}θ˙t​m˙t​dXti​dVti​​=mt​,=−N−1i∑​F(θt​,Xti​)−γmt​,=Vti​dt,=(−Fx​(θt​,Xti​)−γVti​)dt+2γ​dBti​.​

For HOL-MYPGD:

θ˙t=−N−1∑iF(θt,Xti),dXti=Uti dt,dUti=(−Fx(θt,Xti)+γVti) dt,dVti=(−γUti−αVti) dt+2α dBti.\begin{aligned}\dot\theta_t&=-N^{-1}\sum_iF(\theta_t,X_t^i),\qquad\mathrm dX_t^i=U_t^i\,\mathrm dt,\\\mathrm dU_t^i&=(-F_x(\theta_t,X_t^i)+\gamma V_t^i)\,\mathrm dt,\\\mathrm dV_t^i&=(-\gamma U_t^i-\alpha V_t^i)\,\mathrm dt+\sqrt{2\alpha}\,\mathrm dB_t^i.\end{aligned}θ˙t​dUti​dVti​​=−N−1i∑​F(θt​,Xti​),dXti​=Uti​dt,=(−Fx​(θt​,Xti​)+γVti​)dt,=(−γUti​−αVti​)dt+2α​dBti​.​
θ˙t=−N−1∑iF(θt,Xti),dXti=Uti dt,dUti=(−Fx(θt,Xti)+γVti) dt,dVti=(−γUti−αVti) dt+2α dBti.\begin{aligned}\dot\theta_t&=-N^{-1}\sum_iF(\theta_t,X_t^i),\\\mathrm dX_t^i&=U_t^i\,\mathrm dt,\\\mathrm dU_t^i&=(-F_x(\theta_t,X_t^i)+\gamma V_t^i)\,\mathrm dt,\\\mathrm dV_t^i&=(-\gamma U_t^i-\alpha V_t^i)\,\mathrm dt\\&\quad+\sqrt{2\alpha}\,\mathrm dB_t^i.\end{aligned}θ˙t​dXti​dUti​dVti​​=−N−1i∑​F(θt​,Xti​),=Uti​dt,=(−Fx​(θt​,Xti​)+γVti​)dt,=(−γUti​−αVti​)dt+2α​dBti​.​

Write yyy for the implementation phase, an additional symbol distinct from the paper’s sampler ZZZ. Its four coordinates are ((m,V[N]),(θ,X[N]))((m,V^{[N]}),(\theta,X^{[N]}))((m,V[N]),(θ,X[N])) for M-MFPO and (θ,X[N],U[N],V[N])(\theta,X^{[N]},U^{[N]},V^{[N]})(θ,X[N],U[N],V[N]) for HOL. The exact raw norm is ∥y∥max⁡,2=max⁡1≤k≤4∥yk∥L2\|y\|_{\max,2}=\max_{1\le k\le4}\|y_k\|_{\mathrm L^2}∥y∥max,2​=max1≤k≤4​∥yk​∥L2​. The numerical and continuous initial phases coincide.

/-!
# Explicit feasible hypocoercive coefficients

The strict source friction threshold is converted into concrete Young,
auxiliary, metric and decay constants. No coefficient feasibility or
positive-definiteness assertion is assumed. The forces need not be gradients.

namespace PBGSO


/-- The manuscript's displayed square-root friction condition implies
the polynomial threshold used by the coefficient proofs. -/

/-- The squared version of the exact source threshold produces an explicit
Young parameter strictly between zero and one. -/

/-- Both auxiliary dissipation and the projected coefficient have strictly
positive room under the source threshold. -/




section Hilbert
variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

/-- A concrete lower norm constant for the source's actual twisted metric. -/

/-- Young's inequality gives exactly the separate U5 auxiliary estimate
with the explicitly chosen coefficients. -/

/-- A globally monotone and Lipschitz joint force has a completely explicit
positive hypocoercive contraction rate under the source friction threshold.
This is a deterministic drift estimate for the actual metric pairing. -/

end Hilbert

/-- Euclidean product of position and momentum coordinates. -/

/-- The actual source block matrix `[[gamma I,I],[I,2/gamma I]]`
as a bounded linear operator on the Hilbert phase space. -/




/-- Multiplication of the actual block operator by the actual heavy-ball
vector field gives the previously proved scalar pairing identity. -/

end Metric

certified symmetry and quantitative positive definiteness. -/

section Jensen
variable {Ω H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- The square-norm Jensen inequality follows from integrating a
nonnegative squared distance. This supplies the optimiser-force estimate
from its actual Bochner expectation. -/

section HeavyBall
variable {A X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [InnerProductSpace ℝ A] [CompleteSpace A]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [InnerProductSpace ℝ X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X] [Fintype I]

/-- The actual unit-mass heavy-ball optimiser and underdamped sampler.
The observation and negative score are independent maps. Constant diffusion
is arbitrary, allowing the exact source column matrix as a special case. -/

/-- The source position and momentum projections, with the explicitly
chosen positive auxiliary weights. -/

/-- The optimiser vector-field difference really is the heavy-ball block
applied to the state and actual mean-gradient differences. -/

block, without any conservative-potential assumption. -/

/-- End-to-end verification of the source hypocoercive *criterion*, from

friction threshold. No U5, metric, rate-feasibility, Jensen, coupling-gradient
or score-integrability conclusion is assumed in this theorem. This remains
an algebraic/law criterion, separate from an SDE existence or Itô theorem. -/

/-- The source projected field, as an actual map of the Hilbert product. -/

/-- A Lipschitz bound for the complete projected field yields the component

/-- The appendix hypocoercive proposition with its original joint

/-! # Numerical norms of the standard Euclidean particle encoding

inverse has norm at most `sqrt N`. Both values are attained when the particle
and physical coordinate sets are nonempty. -/

/-- The standard Euclidean cloud encoding is nonexpansive into the array sup norm. -/

/-- Exact numeric upper bound for the inverse encoding, including zero dimension. -/

/-- A single nonzero physical coordinate attains the encoding norm. -/

/-- A constant unit particle cloud attains the inverse encoding norm. -/

/-- Empty physical coordinates give the zero encoding operator. -/

/-- Empty physical coordinates give the zero inverse encoding operator. -/

section ForceConstants
variable {A : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℝ A]
  (D : ParticleForceData A (EuclideanSpace ℝ J) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N × J)) N)

/-- The exact displayed empirical force constant in positive physical dimension. -/

/-- The exact displayed sampler force constant in positive physical dimension. -/

/-- The exact sampler force constant when the physical position space is zero. -/
end ForceConstants

end PBGSO.Methods

/-! # Primitive force values in the explicit numerical constants
The actual empirical and coordinatewise L² lifts at zero are constant random
variables.  Under the standard Euclidean cloud encoding their norms reduce

noncomputable section

namespace PBGSO.UniformOrigin
open Methods

variable {Ω A J : Type*} {N : ℕ} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype J]
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℝ A]
  (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
  (D : ParticleForceData A (EuclideanSpace ℝ J) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N × J)) N)

/-- Exact original optimiser force, with no empirical approximation at zero. -/

/-- Actual zero-state sampler lift is the repacked constant cloud. -/

/-- Euclidean flattening of a cloud with one fixed value has the exact sqrt-N norm. -/

/-- The primitive sampler origin norm includes exactly sqrt-N cloud scaling. -/

/-- The actual full HOL drift at zero has the same raw max norm. -/

end PBGSO.UniformOrigin

/-! # Fully constructed time-uniform M-MFPO target guarantee
The source joint monotonicity builds the contracting empirical metric.
Primitive force regularity, actual Gaussian coupling and Picard integral
solutions derive uniform moments, local defects and numerical stability.
-/
noncomputable section
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false
set_option maxHeartbeats 700000
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped NNReal ENNReal InnerProductSpace
namespace PBGSO.FullyUniformMomentum
open Methods ImplementationDynamics FullyConstructedMomentum

variable {A J : Type*} {N : ℕ} [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [InnerProductSpace ℝ A] [CompleteSpace A]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ A]
  [MeasurableSpace A] [BorelSpace A] [SecondCountableTopology A]
  (D : ParticleForceData A (EuclideanSpace ℝ J) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N × J)) N)
  (γ : ℝ)

variable
  (Geometry : TwistedGeometry (HypocoercivePhase A) (HypocoercivePhase (EuclideanSpace ℝ J)))
  (μ : Measure (HypocoercivePhase (EuclideanSpace ℝ J))) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (hμ : MemLp (fun z : HypocoercivePhase (EuclideanSpace ℝ J) ↦ z) 2 μ)
  (a : HypocoercivePhase A) (Variance : ℝ)
  (hVariance : ∀ r, 0 ≤ r →
    (∫ z, ‖(model D γ).observation
      ((model D γ).parameter (AdditiveCanonical.optimizer (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J)
        (momentumForceDynamics D γ) μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r))
      ((model D γ).position z) -
      (model D γ).meanGradient (AdditiveCanonical.law (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J)
        (momentumForceDynamics D γ) μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r)
        (AdditiveCanonical.optimizer (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (momentumForceDynamics D γ)
          μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r)‖ ^ 2
      ∂AdditiveCanonical.law (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (momentumForceDynamics D γ)
        μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r) ≤ Variance)

/-- Coercivity of the constructed source metric in raw kinetic coordinates. -/

/-- Data-only upper norm bound for the constructed metric factor. -/

/-- Actual Brownian increment radius, with the given nonnegative friction. -/

/-- State-independent part of the proved OBABO local Gaussian error. -/

/-- Linear initial-state part of the proved OBABO local Gaussian error. -/

/-- Explicit one-unit exact kinetic radius when started at zero. -/

/-- Data-only transformed zero-start radius `S`. -/

/-- Uniform exact-reference radius, derived by contraction and unit restarts. -/

/-- Linear-radius coefficient absorbed by exact-flow dissipation. -/

/-- Explicit time-uniform numerical coefficient, independent of `h,n`. -/

/-- Explicit positive upper step size; `hγ` only forms the physical friction. -/

/-- Positivity and both uniform bounds for the explicit data-defined constants. -/
/-- The actual raw-state discretisation bound with an explicit coefficient. -/

/-- Final parameter theorem with data-defined coefficient and step size. -/

/-- Backwards-compatible existential form of the explicit guarantee. -/

end PBGSO.FullyUniformMomentum

`‖P‖ ≤ 2` and `‖P⁻¹‖ ≤ 1` without independence assumptions, and constructs the
source-A3 contracting metric with the numerical comparisons
`√lower_N / 2` and `2 * √upper_N`.
-/

import PBGSO.FullyConstructedMomentum
import PBGSO.MomentumUniformParticle
import PBGSO.MethodMetricComparisons
import PBGSO.UniformStepSize

/-! # Fully constructed time-uniform M-MFPO target guarantee
The source joint monotonicity builds the contracting empirical metric.
Primitive force regularity, actual Gaussian coupling and Picard integral
solutions derive uniform moments, local defects and numerical stability.
-/
noncomputable section
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false
set_option maxHeartbeats 700000
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped NNReal ENNReal InnerProductSpace
namespace PBGSO.FullyUniformMomentum
open Methods ImplementationDynamics FullyConstructedMomentum

variable {A J : Type*} {N : ℕ} [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [InnerProductSpace ℝ A] [CompleteSpace A]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ A]
  [MeasurableSpace A] [BorelSpace A] [SecondCountableTopology A]
  (D : ParticleForceData A (EuclideanSpace ℝ J) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N × J)) N)
  (γ : ℝ)

variable
  (Geometry : TwistedGeometry (HypocoercivePhase A) (HypocoercivePhase (EuclideanSpace ℝ J)))
  (μ : Measure (HypocoercivePhase (EuclideanSpace ℝ J))) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (hμ : MemLp (fun z : HypocoercivePhase (EuclideanSpace ℝ J) ↦ z) 2 μ)
  (a : HypocoercivePhase A) (Variance : ℝ)
  (hVariance : ∀ r, 0 ≤ r →
    (∫ z, ‖(model D γ).observation
      ((model D γ).parameter (AdditiveCanonical.optimizer (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J)
        (momentumForceDynamics D γ) μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r))
      ((model D γ).position z) -
      (model D γ).meanGradient (AdditiveCanonical.law (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J)
        (momentumForceDynamics D γ) μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r)
        (AdditiveCanonical.optimizer (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (momentumForceDynamics D γ)
          μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r)‖ ^ 2
      ∂AdditiveCanonical.law (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (momentumForceDynamics D γ)
        μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r) ≤ Variance)

/-- Coercivity of the constructed source metric in raw kinetic coordinates. -/

/-- Data-only upper norm bound for the constructed metric factor. -/

/-- Actual Brownian increment radius, with the given nonnegative friction. -/

/-- State-independent part of the proved OBABO local Gaussian error. -/

/-- Linear initial-state part of the proved OBABO local Gaussian error. -/

/-- Explicit one-unit exact kinetic radius when started at zero. -/

/-- Data-only transformed zero-start radius `S`. -/

/-- Uniform exact-reference radius, derived by contraction and unit restarts. -/

/-- Linear-radius coefficient absorbed by exact-flow dissipation. -/

/-- Explicit time-uniform numerical coefficient, independent of `h,n`. -/

/-- Explicit positive upper step size; `hγ` only forms the physical friction. -/

/-- Positivity and both uniform bounds for the explicit data-defined constants. -/
/-- The actual raw-state discretisation bound with an explicit coefficient. -/

/-- Final parameter theorem with data-defined coefficient and step size. -/

/-- Backwards-compatible existential form of the explicit guarantee. -/

end PBGSO.FullyUniformMomentum
PBGSO/FullyUniformMomentum.lean:77zeroStartMoment
77def zeroStartMoment (hγ : 0 ≤ γ) : ℝ :=78  metricUpper (N := N) Geometry * zeroStartRadius D γ μ hγ

particle integral dynamics, exact restarts, printed Gaussian innovations,

explicit small-step interval. No common force potential is required.

variable (α γ : ℝ) (Geo : TwistedGeometry A (HigherOrderSampler (EuclideanSpace ℝ J)))

  (Variance : ℝ)

    (∫ z, ‖(sourceModel D α γ).observation
      ((sourceModel D α γ).parameter (AdditiveCanonical.optimizer
        (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (higherOrderForceDynamics D α γ)
        μ hμ a (input α) (input_continuous α) (input_zero α) r))
      ((sourceModel D α γ).position z) -

        (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (higherOrderForceDynamics D α γ)
        μ hμ a (input α) (input_continuous α) (input_zero α) r)
        (AdditiveCanonical.optimizer (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J)
          (higherOrderForceDynamics D α γ) μ hμ a
          (input α) (input_continuous α) (input_zero α) r)‖ ^ 2
      ∂AdditiveCanonical.law (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J)
        (higherOrderForceDynamics D α γ) μ hμ a
        (input α) (input_continuous α) (input_zero α) r) ≤ Variance)

        (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (higherOrderForceDynamics D α γ)

        (AdditiveCanonical.optimizer (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J)
          (higherOrderForceDynamics D α γ) μ hμ a
          (input α) (input_continuous α) (input_zero α) r)‖ ^ 2
      ∂AdditiveCanonical.law (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J)
        (higherOrderForceDynamics D α γ) μ hμ a
        (input α) (input_continuous α) (input_zero α) r) ≤ Variance)

Theorem New A — M-MFPO final discretisation bound

Mathematical statement

Assumptions: Extra A4, Extra A5 and the numerical initialization below and the standard Euclidean cloud encoding defined above. Use the paper’s OBABO update and independent Gaussian sampler half-step innovations, with zero optimiser innovations.

Extra assumptions: Extra A4 and Extra A5; γ≥0\gamma\ge0γ≥0, 0<h≤h⋆,M0<h\le h_{\star,M}0<h≤h⋆,M​.

The stationary optimiser state is ϑ⋆=(θ⋆,0)\vartheta_\star=(\theta_\star,0)ϑ⋆​=(θ⋆​,0). Initialise the numerical and continuous interacting systems identically.

For every iteration n∈Nn\in\mathbb Nn∈N, with all constants independent of time and step size,

∥θ^n−θ⋆∥L2≤DMh+κ e−ρnhd0+2+γρκVFN(1−e−ρnh).\|\hat\theta_n-\theta_\star\|_{\mathrm L^2}\le D_M\sqrt h+\sqrt\kappa\,e^{-\rho nh}\mathbf d_0+\frac{2+\gamma}{\rho}\sqrt{\frac{\kappa V_F}{N}}(1-e^{-\rho nh}).∥θ^n​−θ⋆​∥L2​≤DM​h​+κ​e−ρnhd0​+ρ2+γ​NκVF​​​(1−e−ρnh).
∥θ^n−θ⋆∥L2≤DMh+κ e−ρnhd0+2+γρκVFN(1−e−ρnh).\begin{gathered}\|\hat\theta_n-\theta_\star\|_{\mathrm L^2}\le D_M\sqrt h\\+\sqrt\kappa\,e^{-\rho nh}\mathbf d_0\\+\frac{2+\gamma}{\rho}\sqrt{\frac{\kappa V_F}{N}}(1-e^{-\rho nh}).\end{gathered}∥θ^n​−θ⋆​∥L2​≤DM​h​+κ​e−ρnhd0​+ρ2+γ​NκVF​​​(1−e−ρnh).​

The full-state raw maximum-component L2L^2L2 error is also at most the same discretisation term. The factor in the particle floor is the certified response constant used by this endpoint. Constants can depend on fixed population and initial law; they do not grow with iteration count.

  (γ : ℝ)

variable
  (Geometry : TwistedGeometry (HypocoercivePhase A) (HypocoercivePhase (EuclideanSpace ℝ J)))

    (∫ z, ‖(model D γ).observation

        (momentumForceDynamics D γ) μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r))

        (momentumForceDynamics D γ) μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r)
        (AdditiveCanonical.optimizer (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (momentumForceDynamics D γ)
          μ hμ a (input γ) (input_continuous γ) (input_zero γ) r)‖ ^ 2
      ∂AdditiveCanonical.law (ULA.CanonicalBrownian.vectorProbability J) (momentumForceDynamics D γ)

Theorem New B — HOL-MYPGD final discretisation bound

Mathematical statement

Assumptions: Extra A4, Extra A5 and the numerical initialization below and the same cloud encoding. Use the paper’s parameter-first endpoint-force update, its printed coefficients, and the correlated Gaussian innovation triple, with independent time/spatial blocks.

Initialise the numerical and continuous interacting systems identically.

For every iteration n∈Nn\in\mathbb Nn∈N, with all constants independent of time and step size,

The full-state raw maximum-component L2L^2L2 error has the same uniform discretisation coefficient. This is the stationary zero-observation target of the forces actually implemented; a smoothed sampler may have a different target from the original unsmoothed objective. No uniformity in particle count is claimed.

Check the proofs

Use the repository’s pinned Lean and Mathlib versions. From the repository root, fetch the Mathlib cache, compile the development and print the axioms of every main theorem:

lake exe cache get
lake build PBGSO
lake env lean PBGSO/Check.lean

lake build PBGSO checks every proof; the printed axioms should contain only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Readable entry files state each main result with its complete assumptions and conclusion, and their short checked proofs apply the library theorems:

lake env lean standalone/PBGSO/PaperTheorems.lean
lake env lean standalone/PBGSO/NewA.lean
lake env lean standalone/PBGSO/NewB.lean

For a single-file proof that imports only Mathlib, generate the transitive local proof closure:

python3 scripts/check-pbgso-standalone.py --output /tmp/pbgso-standalone --check
lake env lean /tmp/pbgso-standalone/NewA.lean
lake env lean /tmp/pbgso-standalone/NewB.lean

Choose a new or empty output directory. The --check run compiles the exported files in isolation with this project’s compiled proof modules removed from the search path. The exported files contain the original proofs and assumptions, rather than an assumed error estimate. Paper theorem entry file · New A entry file · New B entry file.

Check the statement-to-source correspondence with python3 -B scripts/verify-pbgso.py --require-complete.

Proof roadmap

The roadmap reads from the primitive model at the top to the four paper theorems and the two new discretisation bounds at the bottom. The left columns follow the continuous-time argument: the joint metric of assumption A3 and the local Brownian integral give the stationary product law (Theorem 1), its exponential contraction (Theorem 2), the particle interaction bound (Theorem 3) and the parameter bound (Theorem 4). The right columns follow the numerical argument: the Lipschitz empirical force, the contracting particle metrics built from A3, moments uniform in time and the local errors of the two Gaussian schemes combine into the time-uniform bounds New A and New B. The mathematical argument

The argument below proves the theorems in order. The adjacent panels give the exact Lean statements it rests on and explain how the formal proof assembles them.

01Define the full state, expectations and metric §

Fix a complete optimiser state sss, sampler state zzz, parameter projection PPP, position projection RRR, observation FFF, optimiser response Ψ\PsiΨ, and sampler coefficients b,σib,\sigma_ib,σi​. The mean observation is the actual integral Gν(s)=∫F(P(s),R(z))dνG_\nu(s)=\int F(P(s),R(z))d\nuGν​(s)=∫F(P(s),R(z))dν. Its empirical version is integration against N−1∑iδziN^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{z_i}N−1∑i​δzi​​, which equals the finite observation average for positive particle count. In particular the empirical optimiser uses the same response as the law-level optimiser.

Choose symmetric positive quadratic weights with common bounds 0<ℓ≤u0<\ell\le u0<ℓ≤u, and write κ=u/ℓ\kappa=u/\ellκ=u/ℓ. For a coupling of two sampler laws, add the weighted optimiser square to its expected sampler square to obtain an energy. The joint dissipativity assumption bounds half its derivative by −ρE-\rho E−ρE, including the finite sum of diffusion-difference squares. Every observation and signed work expression used in this assumption must be integrable.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

Model retains independent maps and full auxiliary coordinates. meanGradient_empirical identifies the actual empirical expectation. TwistedJointMonotonicity is the complete joint assumption with its finite-integral domain. These definitions fix the objects used in every subsequent theorem.

02Construct and transfer the stationary reference §

Let the frozen sampler at parameter P(s⋆)P(s_\star)P(s⋆​) have invariant law ν⋆\nu_\starν⋆​. Require integrability of its observation, Gν⋆(s⋆)=0G_{\nu_\star}(s_\star)=0Gν⋆​​(s⋆​)=0, and Ψ(t,s⋆,0)=0\Psi(t,s_\star,0)=0Ψ(t,s⋆​,0)=0. Then adjoining the constant optimiser to this sampler solves the coupled equation. Strong existence on initial-law times Wiener-path space and same-driver uniqueness transfer its law to any original strong solution with the same initial optimiser and sampler law. Thus its complete state has law δs⋆⊗ν⋆\delta_{s_\star}\otimes\nu_\starδs⋆​​⊗ν⋆​. The stationarity claim retains the frozen invariant sampler and strong existence/uniqueness assumptions; it is not inferred from the quadratic inequality alone.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

stationary_product_law_of_weak_frozen constructs the constant-optimiser solution, identifies both it and the original solution with the genuine path-space solution by uniqueness, and converts the resulting marginal identities into the full product-law identity.

03Derive the law contraction from actual stochastic equations §

For each initial coupling, place the two initial samplers with common Brownian coordinates on a canonical source. Localise the raw diffusion by its pathwise squared coefficient energy. Stopped coefficients have finite expected energy, so the actual Brownian integral and its quadratic identity apply. Nested stopping times glue these integrals consistently to the original local equation. Joint dissipativity then gives E′≤−2ρEE'\le-2\rho EE′≤−2ρE, and scalar comparison yields E(T)≤e−2ρTE(0)E(T)\le e^{-2\rho T}E(0)E(T)≤e−2ρTE(0).

Convert the weighted energies to Euclidean ones using ℓ,u\ell,uℓ,u, take square roots, and minimise over initial couplings. With d((s,μ),(s′,ν))2=∥s−s′∥2+W2(μ,ν)2d((s,\mu),(s',\nu))^2=\|s-s'\|^2+W_2(\mu,\nu)^2d((s,μ),(s′,ν))2=∥s−s′∥2+W2​(μ,ν)2, this gives dT≤κe−ρTd0d_T\le\sqrt\kappa e^{-\rho T}d_0dT​≤κ​e−ρTd0​. The passage from arbitrary original probability spaces uses path-source existence and same-driver uniqueness to identify their laws with the canonical ones. There are two explicitly separate domains: primitive coefficient linear growth with measurable/progressive realizations, or constant diffusion with universal finite signed coupling work and Borel fields.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

RawLocalDiffusion supplies only primitive local coefficient data. The two law_distance_decay theorems identify canonical and original laws first, apply their established canonical contraction theorem, and rewrite its conclusion. The linear-growth and finite-work hypotheses remain distinct.

04Control the empirical interaction by independent copies §

Form N>0N>0N>0 independent mean-field references, driven by the same individual Brownian coordinates as the interacting particles. Start with identical optimiser and particle states. If the centred observation variance is at most VVV, independence cancels every cross term in the squared empirical average, leaving variance V/NV/NV/N. An optimiser response bound LΨL_\PsiLΨ​ turns this into the only forcing term in the coupling energy.

Cauchy–Schwarz gives a differential inequality E′≤−2ρE+2cEE'\le-2\rho E+2c\sqrt EE′≤−2ρE+2cE​ with zero initial energy. To handle zeros rigorously, apply the derivative comparison to E+ε2\sqrt{E+\varepsilon^2}E+ε2​ and then let ε↓0\varepsilon\downarrow0ε↓0. Conversion from the weighted energy and the labelled-particle empirical coupling gives interaction error at most LΨρκV/N(1−e−ρT)\frac{L_\Psi}{\rho}\sqrt{\kappa V/N}(1-e^{-\rho T})ρLΨ​​κV/N​(1−e−ρT). The references' product law and the matching with the original native empirical state are proved by construction.

forced_energy_bound performs the positive square-root regularisation. original_finite_particle_interaction_bound builds the native pair internally from the Borel model maps and the actual empirical solution, applies the paired estimate, and rewrites the integral using the proved almost-sure state identity.

06Verify joint dissipativity from the appendix assumptions §

Three criteria produce the joint inequality used above. For separated monotonicity, the optimiser and sampler coupling radii reduce the work to a symmetric two-dimensional quadratic form. Positive diagonal and determinant conditions make its smallest eigenvalue positive; its exact value is (a+b−(a−b)2+c2)/2(a+b-\sqrt{(a-b)^2+c^2})/2(a+b−(a−b)2+c2​)/2.

For projected monotonicity, projected force dissipation and auxiliary work give the block matrices Ko=diag⁡(cI,Dm)K_o=\operatorname{diag}(cI,D_m)Ko​=diag(cI,Dm​), Ks=diag⁡(cI,Dv)K_s=\operatorname{diag}(cI,D_v)Ks​=diag(cI,Dv​), with c=βr−Ao−As>0c=\beta r-A_o-A_s>0c=βr−Ao​−As​>0. Whitening each by its metric matrix gives the positive generalized-eigenvalue rate. Constant diffusion cancels, but signed-work integrability must still be asserted on its finite domain. A finite second moment alone does not suffice: the strongly dissipative drift −x−x3-x-x^3−x−x3 has nonintegrable signed work under a probability law with finite second but infinite fourth moment.

For heavy-ball dynamics, use the quadratic form γ∥q∥2+2⟨q,p⟩+2∥p∥2/γ\gamma\|q\|^2+2\langle q,p\rangle+2\|p\|^2/\gammaγ∥q∥2+2⟨q,p⟩+2∥p∥2/γ. The threshold γ>2L/r\gamma>\sqrt2L/\sqrt rγ>2​L/r​ gives an explicit Young parameter between zero and one, leaving positive position and momentum dissipation and therefore a positive contraction rate. These criteria allow independent forces without a common potential.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

The cited criteria derive their matrix and metric comparisons from the primitive assumptions. The finite-domain theorem adds its work-integrability component explicitly. The scope audit proves the quadratic-versus-quartic obstruction, preventing a silent strengthening of the law theorem's domain.

07Construct the actual particle forces and contracting metric §

The force data provide a nonempty cloud encoding and independent globally Lipschitz parameter and sampler forces. Finite averaging gives the actual empirical mean-force Lipschitz bound; pointwise application and integration lift both forces to square-integrable random variables. Their raw numerical updates agree almost surely with the physical particle formulas.

Source joint dissipativity is then applied to empirical measures and transported through the physical/raw coordinate identification. Factoring the resulting positive quadratic form constructs a bounded linear map CCC and positive mmm such that m∥z∥≤∥Cz∥m\|z\|\le\|Cz\|m∥z∥≤∥Cz∥, with drift pairing ⟨C(x−y),C(f(x)−f(y))⟩≤−ρ∥C(x−y)∥2\langle C(x-y),C(f(x)-f(y))\rangle\le-\rho\|C(x-y)\|^2⟨C(x−y),C(f(x)−f(y))⟩≤−ρ∥C(x−y)∥2. Both the momentum and four-coordinate higher-order schemes use this construction. Numerical contractivity is not a premise.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

meanForce_lipschitz derives the empirical bound from the actual force data. momentum_metric and higherOrder_metric turn empirical source monotonicity into the implemented drift pairing through their coordinate-compatible dynamics. Their returned metric factors supply both coercivity and the dissipation used by the restart estimates.

08Prove moments and absorb accumulated local defects §

For an additive integral trajectory with globally Lipschitz drift, input increments bounded by Ξt\Xi\sqrt tΞt​ on intervals of length at most one, and drift value b0b_0b0​ at zero, the integral equation gives radius eL+1(∥z∥+b0+Ξ)e^{L+1}(\|z\|+b_0+\Xi)eL+1(∥z∥+b0​+Ξ). Compare each unit-time exact trajectory with a zero-start exact trajectory using the same input. Exact drift contraction and a geometric sum give a radius RRR uniform over all time.

For a numerical step AkA_kAk​ and its exact restart Φk\Phi_kΦk​, suppose the actual local error is bounded in the transformed norm by hh(A+B∥Cx∥)h\sqrt h(A+B\|Cx\|)hh​(A+B∥Cx∥). Then, writing ek=∥C(Xk−Y(kh))∥e_k=\|C(X_k-Y(kh))\|ek​=∥C(Xk​−Y(kh))∥, the triangle inequality and ∥CXk∥≤ek+R\|CX_k\|\le e_k+R∥CXk​∥≤ek​+R give ek+1≤(e−ρh+Bhh)ek+(A+BR)hhe_{k+1}\le(e^{-\rho h}+Bh\sqrt h)e_k+(A+BR)h\sqrt hek+1​≤(e−ρh+Bhh​)ek​+(A+BR)hh​. If ρh≤1\rho h\le1ρh≤1 and Bh≤ρ/4B\sqrt h\le\rho/4Bh​≤ρ/4, the coefficient is at most 1−ρh/41-\rho h/41−ρh/4. Summing yields en≤4(A+BR)h/ρe_n\le4(A+BR)\sqrt h/\rhoen​≤4(A+BR)h​/ρ for all nnn, when e0=0e_0=0e0​=0.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

uniform_moment derives the reference radius from the original integral equation and exact-flow contraction. one_step_same_initial_uniform_norm proves the recurrence absorption and divides the final transformed estimate by coercivity. Neither moment bounds nor a final numerical recurrence are assumed in the particle application.

09The time-uniform momentum parameter bound §

The actual OBABO step is compared with its exact integral restart using its implemented force kicks, position drifts and Gaussian thermostats. Primitive Lipschitz force bounds, Brownian second moments and the derived short-time trajectory modulus give a local defect affine in the initial radius and of order hhh\sqrt hhh​. The contracting empirical metric and uniform reference radius supply the preceding absorption argument.

Consequently, on a strictly positive step interval computed from the model and ρ\rhoρ, the numerical-to-exact error is at most KhK\sqrt hKh​ for every iteration. Project to the parameter coordinate and add the exact interacting-particle bound: the total error is numerical bias KhK\sqrt hKh​, initial-law relaxation κe−ρnhd0\sqrt\kappa e^{-\rho nh}d_0κ​e−ρnhd0​, and particle error (LΨ/ρ)κV/N(1−e−ρnh)(L_\Psi/\rho)\sqrt{\kappa V/N}(1-e^{-\rho nh})(LΨ​/ρ)κV/N​(1−e−ρnh), with the response factor fixed by this model. All constants are defined from the actual force, metric, initial state and Brownian data.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

obabo_affine_local_defect derives the actual step-versus-integral defect. FullyUniformMomentum.explicit_parameter_bound supplies the computed admissible step and numerical constant, projects the uniform strong error and adds the constructed exact particle parameter bound by the triangle inequality.

11Verify both continuous and discrete volume statements §

The frictionless phase vector field (p,q)↦(−F(q),p)(p,q)\mapsto(-F(q),p)(p,q)↦(−F(q),p) has zero divergence. A C1C^1C1 force and globally defined actual ODE trajectories give joint C1C^1C1 dependence by compact-orbit localization and Picard construction. The variational equation and zero divergence imply Jacobian determinant one. Uniqueness gives the inverse negative-time flow, and change of variables then proves Lebesgue preservation.

The discrete B–A–B map is a composition of two force kicks and one position drift. Each is a translation shear, so a measurable force suffices for product-Haar preservation by Tonelli and translation invariance. If the force is differentiable in finite dimension, its actual derivatives are triangular block matrices with identity diagonals; the determinant chain rule gives signed determinant one for the full discrete step. These statements concern the frictionless maps.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

The continuous results derive the solution-map regularity, variational identity, inverse and measure pushforward in sequence. The discrete measure and determinant statements have separate regularity hypotheses and apply directly to interwovenBAB.
